ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
At the bottom of a vertical well, an object is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of $v_0 = 15 \mathrm{m/s}$. The object undergoes uniformly decelerated linear motion with an acceleration magnitude of $a = 10 \mathrm{m/s^2}$ during its ascent. The object is caught at the well opening. The displacement of the object in the last 1 second before being caught is $x_1 = 6 \mathrm{m}$.

1. What is the average velocity of the object during the last 1 second before being caught?
2. What is the total time elapsed from when the object is thrown until it is caught?
3. The depth of this vertical well.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: At the bottom of a vertical well, an object is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of $v_0 = 15 \mathrm{m/s}$. The object undergoes uniformly decelerated linear motion with an acceleration magnitude of $a = 10 \mathrm{m/s^2}$ during its ascent. The object is caught at the well opening. The displacement of the object in the last 1 second before being caught is $x_1 = 6 \mathrm{m}$. 1. What is the average velocity of the object during the last 1 second before being caught? 2. What is the total time elapsed from when the object is thrown until it is caught? 3. The depth of this vertical well.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Take upward as positive. The motion is uniformly decelerated with displacement from the release point s(t)=v0 t - (1/2) a t^2 = 15t - 5t^2. 1. In the last 1 s before being caught, the displacement is x1=6 m, so the average velocity over that interval is v_avg=x1/Δt=6/1=6 m/s upward. 2. Let the total time until being caught be T. The displacement in the last second is s(T)-s(T-1). Using s(t)=15t-5t^2: [15T-5T^2] - [15(T-1)-5(T-1)^2] = 6. Simplifying gives 20 - 10T = 6, so T=1.4 s. 3. The well depth is the total upward displacement by time T: h=s(1.4)=15(1.4)-5(1.4)^2=21-9.8=11.2 m.

raw_record.final_cot:
Take upward as positive. The motion is uniformly decelerated with displacement from the release point s(t)=v0 t - (1/2) a t^2 = 15t - 5t^2.

1. In the last 1 s before being caught, the displacement is x1=6 m, so the average velocity over that interval is v_avg=x1/Δt=6/1=6 m/s upward.

2. Let the total time until being caught be T. The displacement in the last second is s(T)-s(T-1). Using s(t)=15t-5t^2:
[15T-5T^2] - [15(T-1)-5(T-1)^2] = 6.
Simplifying gives 20 - 10T = 6, so T=1.4 s.

3. The well depth is the total upward displacement by time T:
h=s(1.4)=15(1.4)-5(1.4)^2=21-9.8=11.2 m.
